63331-the-baptism-of-the-prince-a-sermon.creator: Unknown
63331-the-baptism-of-the-prince-a-sermon.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. rts; the sacred ordinance in which we delight, would be less ridiculed than it is; the fatal mistakes which are made relative to it, would be corrected; and it would soon become, as in primitive times, universally practised. “If infant baptism were more improved,” says Philip Henry, “it would be less disputed.”

arxiv-2102-02045.title: Variants of the A-HPE and large-step A-HPE algorithms for strongly convex problems with applications to accelerated high-order tensor methods
arxiv-2102-02045.creator: M. Marques Alves
arxiv-2102-02045.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. Marques Alves. For solving strongly convex optimization problems, we propose and study the global convergence of variants of the accelerated hybrid proximal extragradient (A-HPE) and large-step A-HPE algorithms of Monteiro and Svaiter [ 21 ] . We prove linear and the superlinear 𝒪 ⁡ ( k − k ⁡ ( p − 1 p + 1 ) ) \mathcal{O}\left(k^{\,-k\left(\frac{p-1}{p+1}\right)}\right) global rates for the proposed variants of the A-HPE and large-step A-HPE methods, respectively.

arxiv-2110-14924.title: Spot and Facula Activity Variations of the Eccentric Detached Eclipsing Binary KIC 8098300 Based on the Time-series Orbital Solutions
arxiv-2110-14924.creator: Hubiao Niu, Jianning Fu, Jiaxin Wang, Chunqian Li
arxiv-2110-14924.description: Abstract The LAMOST spectra and 𝐾𝑒𝑝𝑙𝑒𝑟 \it{Kepler} light curves are combined to investigate the detached eclipsing binary KIC 8098300, which shows the O’Connell effect caused by spot/facula modulation. The radial velocity (RV) measurements are derived by using the tomographic spectra disentangling technology. The mass ratio q = K 1 / K 2 = 0.812 ± 0.007 q=K_{1}/K_{2}=0.812\pm 0.

arxiv-2205-02597.title: Cross-section measurements for the production of a Z Z boson in association with high-transverse-momentum jets in p ​ p pp collisions at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-2205-02597.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-2205-02597.description: Abstract Cross-section measurements for a Z Z boson produced in association with high-transverse-momentum jets ( p T ≥ 100 p_{\mathrm{T}}\geq 100 GeV) and decaying into a charged-lepton pair ( e + ​ e − , μ + ​ μ − e^{+}e^{-},\mu^{+}\mu^{-} ) are presented.

arxiv-2210-13838.title: Multilingual Relation Classification via Efficient and Effective Prompting
arxiv-2210-13838.creator: Yuxuan Chen David Harbecke Leonhard Hennig
arxiv-2210-13838.description: Abstract Prompting pre-trained language models has achieved impressive performance on various NLP tasks, especially in low data regimes. Despite the success of prompting in monolingual settings, applying prompt-based methods in multilingual scenarios has been limited to a narrow set of tasks, due to the high cost of handcrafting multilingual prompts.

arxiv-2303-12366.title: Chern classes in equivariant bordism
arxiv-2303-12366.creator: Stefan Schwede
arxiv-2303-12366.description: Abstract . We introduce Chern classes in U ⁡ ( m ) U(m) -equivariant homotopical bordism that refine the Conner-Floyd–Chern classes in the 𝐌𝐔 \mathbf{MU} -cohomology of B ​ U ​ ( m ) BU(m) . For products of unitary groups, our Chern classes form regular sequences that generate the augmentation ideal of the equivariant bordism rings.

arxiv-2401-01792.title: CoMoSVC: Consistency Model-based Singing Voice Conversion Thanks: Corresponding authors: Wei Xue { weixue@ust.hk}, Yike Guo {yikeguo@ust.hk}
arxiv-2401-01792.creator: Yiwen Lu, Zhen Ye, Wei Xue, Xu Tan, Qifeng Liu, Yike Guo
arxiv-2401-01792.description: Abstract The diffusion-based Singing Voice Conversion (SVC) methods have achieved remarkable performances, producing natural audios with high similarity to the target timbre. However, the iterative sampling process results in slow inference speed, and acceleration thus becomes crucial. In this paper, we propose CoMoSVC, a consistency model-based SVC method, which aims to achieve both high-quality generation and high-speed sampling.

arxiv-2402-12045.title: Broadband parametric amplification in DARTWARS
arxiv-2402-12045.creator: M. Faverzani, P. Campana, R. Carobene, M. Gobbo, F. Ahrens, G. Avallone, C. Barone, M. Borghesi, S. Capelli, G. Carapella, A. P. Caricato, L. Callegaro, I. Carusotto, A. Celotto, A. Cian, A. D’Elia, D. Di Gioacchino, E. Enrico, P. Falferi, L. Fasolo, E. Ferri, G. Filatrella, C. Gatti, D. Giubertoni,
arxiv-2402-12045.description: Abstract Superconducting parametric amplifiers offer the capability to amplify feeble signals with extremely low levels of added noise, potentially reaching quantum-limited amplification. This characteristic makes them essential components in the realm of high-fidelity quantum computing and serves to propel advancements in the field of quantum sensing.

arxiv-2407-01844.title: An Efficient and Sybil Attack Resistant Voting Mechanism
arxiv-2407-01844.creator: Jeremias Lenzi
arxiv-2407-01844.description: Abstract Voting mechanisms are widely accepted and used methods for decentralized decision-making. Ensuring the acceptance or legitimacy of the voting mechanism’s outcome is a crucial characteristic of any robust voting system. Consider the following scenario: A group of individuals wants to choose an option from a set of alternatives without requiring an identification or proof-of-personhood system.

arxiv-2502-01105.title: LayerTracer: Cognitive-Aligned Layered SVG Synthesis via Diffusion Transformer CCS: Computing methodologies Computer vision
arxiv-2502-01105.creator: Yiren Song, Danze Chen, Mike Zheng Shou
arxiv-2502-01105.description: Abstract . Generating cognitive-aligned layered SVGs remains challenging due to existing methods’ tendencies toward either oversimplified single-layer outputs or optimization-induced shape redundancies. We propose LayerTracer, a diffusion transformer based framework that bridges this gap by learning designers’ layered SVG creation processes from a novel dataset of sequential design operations.

arxiv-2502-12156.title: Sampling the full hierarchical population posterior distribution in gravitational-wave astronomy
arxiv-2502-12156.creator: Michele Mancarella, Davide Gerosa
arxiv-2502-12156.description: Abstract We present a full sampling of the hierarchical population posterior distribution of merging black holes using current gravitational-wave data. We directly tackle the most relevant intrinsic parameter space made of the binary parameters (masses, spin magnitudes, spin directions, redshift) of all the events entering the GWTC-3 LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA catalog, as well as the hyperparameters of the underlying population of sources.

arxiv-2503-18098.title: Forward-backward splitting under the light of generalized convexity
arxiv-2503-18098.creator: Konstantinos Oikonomidis, Emanuel Laude, Panagiotis Patrinos
arxiv-2503-18098.description: Abstract In this paper we present a unifying framework for continuous optimization methods grounded in the concept of generalized convexity. Utilizing the powerful theory of Φ \Phi -convexity, we propose a conceptual algorithm that extends the classical difference-of-convex method, encompassing a broad spectrum of optimization algorithms.

arxiv-2510-05504.title: Mechanism Design and Equilibrium Analysis of Smart Contract–Mediated Resource Allocation Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author: Jinho Cha
arxiv-2510-05504.description: Abstract . Decentralized coordination and digital contracting are becoming critical in complex industrial ecosystems, yet existing approaches often rely on ad-hoc heuristics or purely technical blockchain implementations without a rigorous economic foundation. This study develops a mechanism-design framework for smart-contract–based resource allocation that explicitly embeds efficiency and fairness in decentralized coordination.

arxiv-2601-06045.title: Assessing the Carbon Footprint of Virtual Meetings: A Quantitative Analysis of Camera Usage
arxiv-2601-06045.creator: Félix Mortas
arxiv-2601-06045.description: Abstract This paper quantifies the carbon emissions related to data consumption during video calls, focusing on the impact of having the camera on versus off. The findings regarding the environmental benefits achieved by turning off cameras during meetings challenge the claims of some prevalent articles.

arxiv-2604-14959.title: Ultrafast all-optical quantum teleportation
arxiv-2604-14959.creator: Takumi Suzuki, Takaya Hoshi, Akito Kawasaki, Shotaro Oki, Konhi Ichii, Hironari Nagayoshi, Kazuma Takahashi, Takahiro Kashiwazaki, Taichi Yamashima, Asuka Inoue, Takeshi Umeki, Tatsuki Sonoyama, Kan Takase, Warit Asavanant, Mamoru Endo, Akira Furusawa

pmc-10682985.title: Inclusion of Sainfoin in the Concentrate of Finishing Lambs: Fatty Acid Profiles of Rumen, Plasma, and Muscle
pmc-10682985.creator: Clàudia Baila, Margalida Joy, Juan Ramón Bertolín, Susana Alves, Rui Bessa, Mireia Blanco, Sandra Lobón
pmc-10682985.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The effects of sainfoin inclusion (Onobrychis viciifolia) in the finishing concentrate for light lambs on the fatty acid (FA) composition of the ruminal digesta, plasma, and meat were evaluated. Twenty-six weaned male lambs were divided into three groups and fed individually ad libitum for 40 days with one of three concentrates differing in the level of sainfoin inclusion: 0% (0SF), 20% (20SF), and 40% (40SF).

pmc-11680155.title: Efficiency of Bacteriophage-Based Detection Methods for Non-Typhoidal Salmonella in Foods: A Systematic Review
pmc-11680155.creator: Preeda Phothaworn, Chatruthai Meethai, Wanchat Sirisarn, Janet Yakubu Nale, Mikael Skurnik
pmc-11680155.description: Food contamination with non-typhoidal Salmonella (NTS) presents a significant public health risk, underscoring the critical need for rigorous food safety measures throughout the production, distribution, preparation, and consumption stages. Conventional diagnostic strategies are time-consuming and labor-intensive and are thus sub-optimal for throughput NTS detection. Bacteriophages (phages) are highly specialized bacterial viruses and exhibit extreme specificity for their hosts.

pmc-11738599.title: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder and Suicidality: A Case Control Study
pmc-11738599.creator: Swapnil Yadav, V Senthil Kumar Reddi, Jaisoorya Sekharan

pmc-12421605.title: Limited utility of faecal immunochemical testing in a colorectal cancer screening programme for adults with cystic fibrosis: insights from a prospective UK study
pmc-12421605.creator: Aqeem Azam, Karuna Sapru, Andrew M Jones, Dipesh H Vasant, Anne-Marie Kelly, Graham Horsman, Rowland J Bright-Thomas, Javaid Iqbal, Peter J Barry
pmc-12421605.description: ObjectivePeople with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) are at significantly increased risk of colorectal cancer (CRC), prompting international recommendations for earlier screening with colonoscopy. The utility of faecal immunochemical testing (FIT) as a screening adjunct in pwCF remains unclear. This study evaluates FIT’s diagnostic performance and uptake within a CRC screening programme in a UK CF centre.

pmc-12428538.title: Mimicry between adult rove beetles and assassin bug nymphs with unequal defenses: antagonistic or mutualistic?
pmc-12428538.creator: Shinji Sugiura, Masakazu Hayashi
pmc-12428538.description: Defensive mimicry encompasses a continuum ranging from Batesian to Müllerian mimicry. Batesian mimicry involves antagonistic interactions between undefended and defended species, whereas Müllerian mimicry represents mutualistic interactions between species with comparable levels of defense. When mimicry occurs between species with unequal defensive abilities, it is termed quasi-Batesian mimicry, though whether such interactions are antagonistic or mutualistic remains debated.

pmc-12451453.title: Effects of biophilic design-based sports facilities on exercise continuation intention: mediating effects of exercise immersion and moderating effect of environmental awareness
pmc-12451453.creator: Kyongmin Lee, Sung-Jun Park
pmc-12451453.description: The purpose of this study is to empirically analyze how biophilic design elements in sports facilities influence exercise immersion and the intention to continue exercising. Specifically, the study explores the psychological mechanisms underlying this relationship by testing the mediating effect of exercise immersion and the moderating effect of environmental awareness.

pmc-12561628.title: Efficacy and Safety of Topical 5% Cannabidiol Plus Myrcene for the Treatment of Vestibulodynia: A Multi-Centric Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-12561628.creator: Filippo Murina, Giuseppe Ettore, Cecilia Fochesato, Maria Grazia Castiglione, Melania Caruso, Ilenia Fonti, Valeria Savasi
pmc-12561628.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: Vestibulodynia is the prevalent form of vulvodynia, causing burning, irritation, rawness, and dyspareunia sensations. This sensory abnormality suggests sensitization to neuropathic pain. Methods: This was a randomized double-blind trial involving patients who applied a 5% cannabidiol gel with myrcene or a placebo to their vulvar vestibule for 60 days, assessing changes in dyspareunia, pain, and vestibular cotton swab test scores on a 0–10-point VAS scale.

pmc-12643434.title: Case Report: Scalpel Sign and Dorsal Arachnoid Cyst—The Importance of an Accurate Diagnosis
pmc-12643434.creator: Matteo Bonetti, Michele Frigerio, Mario Muto, Federico Maffezzoni, Serena Miglio
pmc-12643434.description: Background and Clinical Significance: Thoracic dorsal arachnoid web (DAW) is a rare intradural extramedullary condition characterized by a thin band of arachnoid tissue compressing the dorsal spinal cord. A hallmark imaging feature is the “scalpel sign”, which refers to anterior displacement of the thoracic spinal cord with dorsal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) accumulation, producing a sagittal profile resembling a surgical scalpel.

pmc-12919384.title: A beginner’s guide to the clinical approach and key concepts of glomerular disease: a mini review
pmc-12919384.creator: Suwasin Udomkarnjananun, Talerngsak Kanjanabuch, Dennis A. Hesselink
pmc-12919384.description: Glomerular disease is a common issue in nephrology, where prompt diagnosis and appropriate treatment are crucial to halting disease progression and preventing the development of chronic kidney disease or end-stage kidney disease. The initial approach and differential diagnosis remain essential clinical skills for ensuring timely investigation and management.

pmc-13183603.title: How does type 2 diabetes modify the risk of Alzheimer's disease?
pmc-13183603.creator: G T Sutherland, A Chen, H‐T Nguyen‐Hao, H Mundell, E Aladyeva, M J Hofer, O Harari, S M Twigg
pmc-13183603.description: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) are both increasing exponentially worldwide. T2D has also been identified as one of 14 modifiable risk factors for dementia, but the mechanism is unknown. T2D could promote dementia via vascular or AD neuropathological changes, and mechanistic hypotheses include central insulin resistance and T2D's peripheral inflammation promoting central inflammation.

pmc-13353419.title: Low-intensity stimulation drives macrophage efferocytosis via ACSL4 lipid remodeling and CCL9-CCR1 signaling for tendon-bone healing
pmc-13353419.creator: Juncheng Yao, Yuhao Wu, Xuan Wang, Jiexin Zhang, Yan Shao, Huabin Chen, Haiyan Zhang, Haobin Li, Jianying Pan, Yitao Zhao, Daozhang Cai, Denghui Xie, Chun Zeng
pmc-13353419.description: The mechanisms underlying exercise rehabilitation–induced tendon-bone healing remain unclear. Using a mouse model of anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, we found that low-intensity mechanical stimulation promoted macrophage M2 polarization, phagocytosis, and efferocytosis at the tendon-bone interface via acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4)–mediated lipid metabolism reprogramming. Acsl4 silencing reduced fatty acid oxidation and efferocytosis, impairing exercise rehabilitation–induced tendon-bone healing.

pmc-13487262.title: Enhanced antibacterial performance of chili pepper seed protein hydrolysates by high hydrostatic pressure assisted enzymatic hydrolysis on Staphylococcus aureus: structural basis and mechanistic insights
pmc-13487262.creator: Sidi Liu, Yue Han, Yiyi He, Yunkai Zhang, Yu Xiong, Wenshu Huang, Dong Yang, Liang Zhao, Xiaojun Liao
pmc-13487262.description: Antibiotic resistance of Staphylococcus aureus threatens public health. Plant by-product protein hydrolysates contain antibacterial peptides as antibiotic alternatives, but compact native protein structures restrict hydrolysis efficiency and antibacterial fragment release. This study applied high hydrostatic pressure (HHP) to assist papain hydrolysis of chili pepper seed protein (PSP) to improve hydrolysis efficiency and antibacterial activity.
